title: The Last Crown Anew
premise: Emrys Fairweather, a mercenary bound by an oath to a god who fell silent a decade ago, has spent his life in the Godless Valley, the one place where magic cannot reach. When a feral child named Wren arrives at his door speaking the First Tongue, Emrys learns she is the last vessel of the god's voice — and that the king of Aldermarch has been hollowed out and worn like armor by the thing that silenced the divine. Pursued by crown inquisitors and haunted by the truth that his own oath helped seal the god away, Emrys must carry Wren to the capital, unbind the king, and choose between restoring a god who may demand everything or letting the world stay godless. In the end he breaks his oath rather than renew it, freeing both king and child, and builds a new kind of covenant — one sworn between people instead of powers.
about_author: Juniper Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing medieval oaths and curse-formulae before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about broken promises and the families people build from the wreckage.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Nothing Follows
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. A routine bounty job ends badly when Emrys's old war-blessing fails mid-fight, nearly killing him. Returning to his cabin at the valley's edge, he reflects on ten years of silence from his god and the oath-scar that still itches. Emotional beat: weary resignation, a man surviving on habit rather than faith.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. During a snowstorm, a girl of eight or nine appears at his door, barefoot, unafraid, speaking a language no one should know. When she touches his oath-scar, it burns — and for one heartbeat, Emrys hears his god's voice again. Emotional beat: terror and longing colliding; the first crack in his isolation.

chapters.title: First Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Through the child's eyes we learn she fled something in the capital called 'the Wearing,' guided by a voice that went quiet as she crossed into the valley. She cannot explain how she knows things. Emrys feeds her, gruffly. Emotional beat: two lonely creatures circling each other, neither able to name what they need.

chapters.title: Inquisitors at the Ford
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Crown inquisitors arrive hunting a 'heretical vessel,' led by the courteous, chilling Serel Vane. Emrys lies for the first time in years and realizes he's already chosen a side. He sends Wren ahead with a neighbor's mule and prepares to buy time. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment; the law is not justice.

chapters.title: What the Oath Cost
chapters.summary: POV Emrys, flashback-heavy. We learn the full history: during the Godswar, Emrys's company swore the Binding Oath that sealed the gods' voices away to end the burning of the world — and his god consented to be silenced. The scar is the receipt. Emotional beat: guilt reframed; he wasn't abandoned, he was complicit.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Crossing the valley boundary, magic floods back — and so does pursuit. Wren's borrowed power flares, healing a dying farmer but aging her hands like an old woman's. Emrys sees the price of survival written on her skin. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by dread; power always bills someone.

chapters.title: The Hollow King's Men
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. In the market town of Brackenfell, they find posters bearing Wren's face and hear rumors: the king has not slept in three years, and his edicts grow stranger. An old comrade, Captain Ilsa Vey, warns Emrys that Vane reports directly to the throne. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; the enemy is the state itself.

chapters.title: A Family Assembled From Strays
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Vey (new POV). Ilsa deserts rather than report them, bringing her cart, her crossbow, and her bitter humor. The trio becomes an accidental family around a campfire — Wren laughing for the first time. Emotional beat: warmth earned against odds; found family taking shape.

chapters.title: The Temple of the Quiet God
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. They shelter in a ruined temple where Emrys once took his oath. Wren reads the First Tongue inscriptions aloud: the Binding was meant to be temporary, a tourniquet — but someone used it to seize the gods' power. The crown didn't just survive the silence; it caused it. Emotional beat: revelation and fury.

chapters.title: Serel Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Serel Vane. Vane corners them, revealing he knows exactly what Wren is — because he helped make the Wearing. He offers Emrys absolution: surrender the child, and the crown will pardon the deserters. His sincerity is the horror; he believes he saved the world. Emotional beat: temptation and moral clarity refusing it.

chapters.title: Night of Knives
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Vane's strike team attacks at night. Ilsa is gravely wounded holding the bridge; Wren, terrified, unleashes the god-voice and unmakes three men — then collapses, her hair going white at the temples. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh; innocence spent like coin.

chapters.title: The Leech and the Litany
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. A hedge-healer named Odji saves Ilsa but tells Emrys the truth: every time Wren channels the god, she pays in years. There are perhaps three workings left in her before nothing remains. Emotional beat: quiet devastation; love means counting someone else's remaining days.

chapters.title: The Capital of Ash Bells
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. They enter Aldermarch's capital disguised among pilgrims. The city is obedient and afraid; bells ring hourly 'for the king's rest' though the king never rests. Ilsa sees her old regiment patrolling for the crown and grieves what loyalty became. Emotional beat: infiltration tension; home as hostile territory.

chapters.title: The Court of the Worn Man
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Using Ilsa's credentials, Emrys gains audience and sees the king: a puppet of meat and ceremony, eyes like shuttered windows, the crown fused to his skull. The thing wearing him speaks through his mouth — and recognizes Emrys's oath-scar instantly. Emotional beat: cold horror; the enemy knows him by name.

chapters.title: Confession Before the Fire
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Safe in the undercity with smuggler allies, Emrys confesses everything to Wren and Ilsa: his role in the Binding, his decade of hiding. Wren takes his scarred hand and says the god never blamed him — it chose him because he would understand cost. Emotional beat: catharsis; shame met with grace.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The plan: Wren must speak the counter-litany while touching the crown, which requires standing inside the throne room during the Ash Bell ceremony. Odji's warning hangs over everything — this will take nearly all of her. Wren volunteers anyway, saying she was sent to finish it. Emotional beat: terrible resolve; a child choosing sacrifice.

chapters.title: Bells for the King's Rest
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The ceremony begins. Vane springs his trap — he expected them — and Ilsa holds the doors with the smugglers while Emrys fights toward the throne through consecrated fire. Emotional beat: climax igniting; chaos, loyalty under pressure, everything staked.

chapters.title: The Thing That Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. At the throne, the usurper reveals itself: the first oath-breaker, a man who devoured his god and has been starving ever since, wearing kings as masks. It offers Emrys his god's voice back if he kneels. Emotional beat: the ultimate temptation; the whole book's theme in one offer.

chapters.title: The Counter-Litany
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren reaches the crown and begins the rite as her body fails — hair white, veins luminous, years draining. Emrys refuses the usurper's bargain and adds his broken oath to her litany, shattering the Binding from the inside. The god's voice returns to the world like a tide. Emotional beat: climax resolved through shared sacrifice, not solo heroics.

chapters.title: After the Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The usurper, unmasked and unfed, crumbles. The king wakes, old and weeping and free. Magic returns unevenly to the world; some rejoice, some flee. Ilsa carries Wren's small, breathing body from the smoking hall, refusing to believe the cost was total. Emotional beat: exhausted grief with a thread of hope.

chapters.title: What the God Asked For
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The restored god comes to Emrys not with demands but a question: what covenant now? Emrys answers — no more bindings, only promises kept between equals. The god consents to whisper rather than command. Wren wakes, aged beyond her years but alive, her debt paid down to a single silver strand. Emotional beat: reconciliation; divinity humbled into partnership.

chapters.title: The Last Crown Anew
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Spring. The king abdicates to a council; Vane stands trial by the very law he twisted. Emrys, Ilsa, and Wren return to the valley cabin — no longer hiding, simply home. Wren plants a tree over the buried oath-stone. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; family chosen, justice made, survival finally worth its price.
